svg.title: Three paths out of a private subnet, and what each one bills
svg.desc: Traffic from a private subnet to an AWS service can leave through a NAT gateway, a gateway endpoint, or an interface endpoint. The NAT gateway bills an hourly rate plus a per-gigabyte processing charge. Gateway endpoints are free but serve only S3 and DynamoDB and cannot be reached from on-premises networks. Interface endpoints are billed per endpoint per Availability Zone plus a per-gigabyte processing charge, and are reachable from on-premises and other Regions.
svg.text: ONE PRIVATE SUBNET, THREE WAYS OUT
Instance in a private subnet calls an AWS API
NAT gateway
The default when nobody decided.
$0.045 per hour
$0.045 per GB processed
Billed on traffic that never leaves the
AWS network. Partial hours bill as full.
Gateway
endpoint
No hourly charge.
No per-GB charge.
S3 and DynamoDB
only.
Interface endpoint (PrivateLink)
Every other service, and S3 too.
billed per endpoint, per AZ, per hour
$0.01 per GB (first 1 PB / month)
Reachable from on-premises and from
another Region. The other two are not.
THE ORDER THE DECISION IS ACTUALLY MADE IN
1 · Is it S3 or DynamoDB, called from inside the VPC?
Then a gateway endpoint carries it for nothing. This is free money and is skipped surprisingly often.
2 · Is it a chatty service — ECR, CloudWatch Logs, SSM, Secrets Manager, STS?
Then an interface endpoint usually beats paying NAT processing on the same bytes. Volume decides.
3 · Does anything still need the public internet?
OS patching, third-party APIs, package registries. That is what the NAT gateway is for — and only that.
The hybrid trap: a gateway endpoint cannot be reached from on-premises
AWS states plainly that gateway endpoints “do not allow access from on premises” and do not work from another Region. A hybrid estate needs an interface endpoint as well — not instead.
Keep both, and let each carry what it is cheapest at

Enabling private DNS only for inbound endpoints keeps in-VPC traffic on the free gateway endpoint while on-premises traffic uses the billed interface endpoint. It is the default, and it requires the gateway endpoint to exist.
